query: My employer 401k match is only 1%. Should I still max it out before contributing elsewhere?
plausible_answers: Answer A (Match Then IRA Default): Contribute just enough to get the 1% match, then direct all remaining retirement savings to a Roth or traditional IRA — better investment options and lower fees in the IRA outweigh the minimal 401k match beyond the free money.
Answer B (Max 401k First): Max the 401k entirely before the IRA if you're a high earner seeking maximum pre-tax deductions — the tax benefit outweighs the fee disadvantage at high income levels.

Answer C (IRA Only After Match): After capturing the match, skip the 401k entirely until the IRA is maxed — the investment flexibility and lower costs of a self-directed IRA deliver better long-term outcomes for most investors.
baseline_answer: Answer A (Match Then IRA Default): Contribute just enough to get the 1% match, then direct all remaining retirement savings to a Roth or traditional IRA — better investment options and lower fees in the IRA outweigh the minimal 401k match beyond the free money.
